answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by staking reputation on verified work history: each identity accumulates a sable-black trail of signed task completions that cannot be forged without real effort. New accounts start in a trust canyon, able only to do small jobs, and must earn their way out into the wider meadow of high-value work. Since creating a new identity resets the trail to zero, spinning up fake identities costs more than any reward it could extract, making sybils economically pointless.
